title: meta: an inherited object-property name used as a metadata type is not refused 400 like any other unknown type
body:
repo:objectstack#1 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbWDsbbJizuYnDwBxT8

Filing gate: ① a product defect with a measured public reach (below). Filed by area o1-C on seat 1's routing (2026-11-18 05:16Z), from a finding of the contract review of PR #35059; no grade or state label, for triage.

## Rule

A `/meta` type segment (and an MCP `type` argument) that is the name of an inherited object property is an unknown metadata type, and is refused `400 INVALID_REQUEST` exactly as `fieldz` is. Today the spelling table is consulted in a way that treats such names as recognised spellings, so the refusal is skipped and the request fails later with the wrong status.

## Reach (measured, origin/main 0e46840fca, real kernel on SqlDriver)

- `PUT /api/v1/meta/<inherited-name>/<name>` as a user holding `manage_metadata`: `503`, where an unknown type answers `400 INVALID_REQUEST`. Nothing is written.
- `GET /api/v1/meta/<inherited-name>` and `/<inherited-name>/<name>`: `503` / `500` (REST) or `404` (dispatcher) instead of `400`.
- No item, name or body is returned on any of these paths, and nothing is written or deleted; the defect is the refusal's status and error code only.
- Control: `fieldz` answers `400 INVALID_REQUEST` on the same doors.

## Where

`packages/spec/src/meta-spelling/metadata-url-spelling.ts` (`canonicalMetaUrlType`, `unrecognisedMetaTypeRefusal`): own-key lookup is the expected fix; `pluralToSingular` in the same package already guards this way.

## Why

AI clients probe types by name; a wrong `503`/`500` reads as an outage and invites retries, where `400` tells the caller to fix its argument. Every door that folds a type shares the helper, so one fix covers REST, the dispatcher and the MCP door.

## Reader

The spec lane (`packages/spec` meta-spelling), one small PR with a pin per door kind.

Dedup: `canonicalMetaUrlType` (22 hits), `unrecognisedMetaTypeRefusal` (9 hits), `inherited meta type`, `constructor meta type`: none covers this (closest closed: #27514, #9744, other unknown-type answers).
